The first-2-minute data is mixed: 43 buyers ex-agent, but top-5 hold 39% and a launch bot is present. Last 15 min is net buying (8.7 SOL net flow, +15.7%), but the 15% drawdown from the 30-min high means momentum is fading. Pool depth of 117 SOL is adequate for a $20 ticket.

memos.scout:
The strongest honest case rests on the last 15 minutes and the early buyer spread. Net flow was +8.69 SOL over 15 minutes, with 16 buyers, 26 sellers, and about $5.2k volume. The coin is up 57% over 30 minutes and sits 15% below its 30-minute high, so it has held most of its gains. The first two minutes after graduation drew 43 buyers outside our agent, with a top-5 buyer share of 39% and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.16, which suggests broad early participation. No airdrop dump was seen, and the class is ORGANIC, which avoids the factory base rate.

The case is weakened by the curve data. The bundle share of 1.0 and a top-3 share of 81% point to coordinated early buying, and the completer share above 1 is unusual. Sellers outnumber buyers in the last 15 minutes, and sell SOL (17.5) is two-thirds of buy SOL (26.2). With only 117 SOL of pool depth and a round trip costing up to 5%, I can't identify demand that is clearly durable for the next 30-60 minutes. I'd call this a weak buy case, and given the bundling signal I'd lean toward skipping.
memos.skeptic: Biggest risk: a bundled launch that is now distributing into a 30-minute pump. The curve data shows bundle_share 1.0 and top3_share 0.81, with only 8 curve buyers, so the supply was concentrated from the start. The first 2 minutes post-graduation had a launch bot present, with top5 buyers holding 39% of volume and a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.16 (sells are only a fraction of buys, which looks clean on the surface). Yet over the last 15 minutes, sell_sol (17.5) is two-thirds of buy_sol (26.2), with 26 sellers against 16 buyers, and the price is already 15% off its 30-minute high after a 57% run. That pattern fits early holders taking profit into thin buying. At 117 SOL pool depth, a $20 round trip faces 1.4-5.1% friction, so even a modest pullback erases the edge. Verdict: skip.
